title: JFK letter to CIA Director McCone requesting UFO data
summary: Jesse Michels tells of JFK letter to CIA Director McCone requesting UFO data, about 1963 (released 2006) at Washington, D.C., and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: But there is a letter that was supposedly declassified due to a Freedom of Information Act request in 2006. It was from JFK to the director of the CIA at the time, John McCone. Its date? November 12th, 1963, just ten days before the president's assassination.

1963 just 10 days before JFK's death
tellings.difference: This telling describes the letter as asking about "unknowns in space" and does not give the 2006 release year or credit an archivist.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings describe the same document: JFK's November 12, 1963 letter to CIA Director John McCone asking about unknowns/UFO data, said to have been released through FOIA, dated ten days before his death.

as_told.title: JFK memo to CIA director McCone on unknowns, 10 days before his death

tellings.difference: Adds the stated purpose of coordinating with the Soviets and credits John Greenwald.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the November 12, 1963 letter in which JFK asks CIA Director McCone for data on unknowns.

related.note: Both are about JFK asking CIA Director McCone for UFO information in 1963. This telling has it as a request for a full briefing on June 5, 1963, while the story has it as a letter dated November 12, 1963.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is a letter from President John F. Kennedy to John McCone, then head of the CIA, America's foreign intelligence agency, that was released in 2006 through the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. Michels says the letter is dated November 12, 1963, ten days before Kennedy was killed, and asks for all data on unknown objects, which in one telling he says was so the US could work with the Soviets on the matter, though he often adds that where the letter came from is disputed. If it is real, it would mean a president was pressing for UFO information just before his death.
